title: VALUE vs NUMBERVALUE: parsing text to numbers, and locales
meta_desc: VALUE vs NUMBERVALUE: converting text to numbers, and why NUMBERVALUE matters when decimal/thousands separators differ by locale. Executed in LibreOffice Calc; Excel and Google Sheets behavior per official docs.
intro: Both turn text that looks like a number into a real number so you can do math. VALUE uses your spreadsheet's locale settings to interpret separators; NUMBERVALUE lets you SPECIFY the decimal and grouping characters explicitly — which is the whole point when you're cleaning data that came from a different region.

cols: You pass the decimal and group separators as arguments
Excel 2013+, Google Sheets, LibreOffice (verified by execution)

when.use_when: The text already matches your machine's locale — the common case for a quick =VALUE(A2) to un-text a number, or letting arithmetic coerce it (A2*1).

Imported data uses different separators than your locale (a German CSV's "1.234,56", or thousands-spaces), so you must state the decimal and grouping characters to parse it reliably regardless of machine settings.

compat_note: Both execute correctly in every LibreOffice version we test; Google Sheets matches in our executed run; Excel behavior matches per Microsoft's documentation, which we do not execute. NUMBERVALUE needs Excel 2013+ but has been in Google Sheets and LibreOffice throughout our tested range. The reverse trip — number to formatted text — is TEXT; and for cleaning stray currency symbols first, see the convert-currency-text-to-a-number recipe.
